subject: Committed TPS and SLO mapping for Unitech capacity commitment
messages:
From: Sara Denton <sara.denton@unitech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for committed throughput

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for jumping on this. Procurement needs a clear mapping from our committed monthly spend to an expected tokens-per-second (TPS) baseline and what SLOs that baseline will meet (p99 latency targets, typical tail). We're targeting a dedicated pool for peak production traffic in Q1.

Quick background: our plan is to run a short-completion, interactive assistant (avg output ~90 tokens, 1.5 reqs/user/min) for ~600 concurrent users at launch. We want a 99th percentile latency of <350ms for common prompts, and graceful degradation to <700ms during transient spikes.

Can you provide an initial recommended config (GPU family + count), expected sustained TPS, suggested headroom for burst, and any notes we should include in the procurement doc? I've attached our token profile CSV.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Denton
Head of Platform
Unitech

Attachment: unitech_token_profile.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Denton <sara.denton@unitech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for committed throughput

Sara —

Thanks for the profile and SLAs. I've run a quick back-of-envelope against the numbers in your CSV and sketched an initial mapping below. This is a proposal for procurement language and a starting point for Dedicated sizing; we'll validate with a short perf run on your representative prompt set.

Summary (prelim):
- Workload: interactive assistant, avg completion 90 tokens, 600 concurrent users, 1.5 reqs/user/min => ~900 reqs/min total => 15 reqs/sec.
- Tokens/sec estimate (client-side): 15 reqs/sec * 90 tokens = 1,350 tokens/sec sustained.
- Allowing for input tokens, network overhead, and variability, assume 1.6x token amplification => ~2,160 effective tokens/sec.

Estimated per-GPU throughput (conservative):
- H100 (80GB, quantized path): ~2,200 - 3,200 tokens/sec for short completions at modest batch sizes. Use 2,200 tps as baseline for SLO planning.
- A100 (40GB): ~1,200 - 1,800 tps. Use 1,300 tps baseline.

SLO-fit and recommended commitment:
- Baseline sustained needed: 2,160 tps (see above).
- With H100 baseline 2,200 tps, 1 x H100 covers the sustained tokens but leaves no headroom for spikes or background tasks.
- Recommendation: reserve 3 x H100 nodes for committed pool (nominal sustained capacity ~6,600 tps). Rationale: provides ~3x headroom which keeps 99p latency inside target under steady-state increases and allows autoscale buffer.

Burst/autoscale policy suggestion:
- Allow burst to a shared overflow pool (Dedicated burst) up to +50% for short periods (60–120s).
- Configure autoscale cooldown to 90s and a max scale of 6 H100-equivalents for safety during launch waves.

Procurement language to include:
- Committed capacity: 3 H100-equivalents reserved (baseline), additional burst up to 6 H100-equivalents billed at burst rate.
- Expected sustained TPS per commitment: ~6,600 tps baseline (3 x 2,200).
- SLA: p99 latency targeting <350ms under sustained baseline; transient spikes handled by burst/fallback with graceful degradation to <700ms.

Attachments: I'm attaching a quick workbook with the numbers and a draft proposal PDF for procurement. We'll refine after a perf run.

Next steps: Karthik — can you sanity-check the conservative per-GPU tps I used and add anything about quantization/kv-cache effects? Marissa — can you add pricing language and note the billing cadence assumptions?

Best,
Vivek
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tps_modeling_workbook.xlsx, unitech_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask for committed throughput (internal notes)

Quick internal note / sanity checks. I'm using measurements from our H100 fleet on short-completion workloads (avg 64-128 tokens):
- Measured median per-H100 throughput (short paths, batching enabled): ~2.6k tps. Tail p99 throughput (no aggressive batching) closer to 1.9k tps.
- KV-cache warm hits increase effective throughput by ~15-25% for contextual prompts; if Unitech will often re-use recent context, we can count on that benefit.
- Quantized 4-bit paths help on cost but may reduce peak tps by ~5-10% in our runs; recommend validating on their prompt set.

Given Sara's latency goals, Vivek's 3x baseline is conservative but sensible for a production launch. My recommended adjustments:
- Commit 2 H100s as guaranteed (covers sustained with modest buffer assuming KV-cache hit), with 1 H100 reserved as 'hot standby' in the Dedicated pool to keep p99 headroom.
- Configure a hard cap at 6 H100s for burst, with automated fallback to a slightly cheaper A100-equivalent model if H100 capacity is exhausted (fallthrough policy).
- If Unitech opts for a less expensive commit (2 x H100-equivalent), include an explicit performance validation window (2-week perf run with representative traffic) and an SLA ladder tied to observed p99.

I'll populate the workbook with the p99/baseline curves and signaling thresholds.

—Karthik

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Denton <sara.denton@unitech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T12:37:00-08:00
Subject: Committed TPS and SLO mapping for Unitech capacity commitment

Sara —

Appended below is the recommended commitment and procurement wording after an internal review. This represents our conservative, production-ready default; if you'd like a lower-cost option we can offer a 2x H100-equivalent baseline with a validation window.

Recommendation (final):
- Committed baseline: 2 x H100-equivalents guaranteed + 1 x H100-equivalent hot standby (total 3 H100-equivalents reserved).
  - Effective baseline TPS (conservative): 2 x 2,200 + 1 x 2,200 standby = 6,600 tps nominal baseline.
  - Expected to meet p99 <350ms under expected traffic with KV-cache assumptions; p99 could degrade toward ~500–600ms if KV-cache is cold and sustained load spikes occur.
- Burst policy: autoscale to up to 6 H100-equivalents for brief intervals (60–180s). Burst billing applies beyond baseline.
- Fallback policy: if H100s exhausted, route to A100-equivalents with clear notice and expected higher latency (~+30%) and lower TPS.

Optional lower-cost offer: 2 x H100-equivalents baseline (no standby) + 2-week validation run. If metrics confirm p99 <350ms, convert to steady state; otherwise ramp to recommended 3-equivalent baseline.

Procurement snippet you can paste: 
"Redwood will provide a Dedicated pool with a guaranteed baseline of 2 x H100-equivalents plus 1 hot standby H100-equivalent (3 H100-equivalents total). The baseline provides an expected sustained throughput of approximately 6,600 tokens/sec and is sized to meet Unitech's p99 latency target of <350ms under normal operating conditions. Short-term bursts up to 6 H100-equivalents are supported and billed at the agreed burst rate. In the event of capacity constraints, traffic will fail over to A100-equivalents with an expected degradation in latency and throughput as documented in the attached performance appendix."

Next steps:
- Sara: confirm whether Unitech wants the conservative 3-equivalent baseline or the 2-equivalent trial option.
- Marissa: I'll need the formal pricing language for both options so we can include it in the SOW.
- Karthik: let's schedule a 2-hour perf run the week of Nov 30 if they choose the trial.

I'll attach the workbook and proposal to the procurement email now.

Best,
Vivek

Attachment: unitech_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf, tps_modeling_workbook.xlsx
